## Extract homologous gene lists
```{r}
#combine all the jaccard similarities
rbind(
tibble(all_jac=homologous_modules$jaccard.index.clown.goby),
tibble(all_jac=homologous_modules$jaccard.index.clown.danio),
tibble(all_jac=homologous_modules$jaccard.index.clown.manini),
tibble(all_jac=homologous_modules$jaccard.index.clown.grouper))->all_jac

#long version of data
homologous_modules %>% pivot_longer(contains("col"), names_to = "species.col", values_to = "col") %>% 
  pivot_longer(contains("jaccard"), names_to = "jaccard.comp", values_to = "jaccard.val") %>% 
  pivot_longer(contains("pres"),names_to = "pres.comp", values_to = "pres.val")->homologous_long

#filter out the top 30% homologous module comparisons
homologous_long %>% filter(jaccard.val >= quantile(all_jac$all_jac,0.70)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(species.col, col) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = species.col, values_from = col) %>% 
  unnest(cols = c(col.goby, col.danio, col.manini, col.grouper, col.clown)) %>% 
  distinct(col.goby, col.danio, col.manini, col.grouper, col.clown)->homologous_filtered

homologous_gene_list<-function(mod){ 
  #this functions takes stable module assignments e.g. from clown and then combines all the other species and collates the data 
  #to obtain lists of genes shared between all 'homologous' modules
  #these genes can be though to represent conserved processes across species
  #annotating them shows which key processes have a high degree of co-regulation among species
  #select one column with stable annotation
  #homologous_filtered %>% filter(col.clown==mod)->one_col
  non_homologous_filtered %>% filter(col.clown==mod)->one_col #Use for non-homologus modules

  #get the list of 'homologus' columns in other species
  one_col %>% distinct(col.goby) %>% pull(col.goby)->goby_col_list
  one_col %>% distinct(col.danio) %>% pull(col.danio)->danio_col_list
  one_col %>% distinct(col.manini) %>% pull(col.manini)->manini_col_list
  one_col %>% distinct(col.grouper) %>% pull(col.grouper)->grouper_col_list
  
  #Here I get the genes from the above list of modules
  danio_col_get<-function(c1){danio_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(module==c1) %>% return()}
  
  manini_col_get<-function(c1){manini_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(module==c1) %>% return()}
  
  grouper_col_get<-function(c1){grouper_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(module==c1) %>% return()}
  
  goby_col_get<-function(c1){goby_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(module==c1) %>% return()}
  
  #I then combine all the genes from the list of modules above to select the genes that are present in all the modules. 
  #e.g. The orange clownfish module has significant overlap between darkgrey, tan, and green modules in zebrafish. While in manini, it has significant overlaps between darkturquoise, greenyellow, red, and green modules.
  #I take the genes from the zebrafish set and the manini set and combine them to only include genes that are present in both. I do this for the other two species.
  #The result is a list of genes that are, to an extent, co-expressed together. I say to an extent because, the same gene might not always be co-expressed together in the same module, in all species. 
  #For instance, look at the top ten genes in the common_all object. You'll see that all these genes are expressed together in the darkgrey module in zebrafish, but in manini some are expressed together in the greenyellow module, while some are expressed together in the red, or green module.  Essentially, this filtering approach captures genes that, on an average tend to be co-expressed together. This is expected considering they are different species with different developmental trajectories, but the fact that we can find a large degree of overlap between gene interactions across species highlights the presence of a common regulatory underpinning between orthologs. However, studying the deviations and specific modification of the network in each species will provide valuable information regarding the interplay of gene expression and regulatory evolution. 
  
inner_join(
    purrr::map(danio_col_list,danio_col_get) %>% list_rbind(),
    purrr::map(manini_col_list,manini_col_get) %>% list_rbind(), by = "gene", suffix = c(".danio", ".manini")) %>% 
    inner_join(purrr::map(grouper_col_list,grouper_col_get) %>% list_rbind(), by = "gene") %>% 
    inner_join(purrr::map(goby_col_list,goby_col_get) %>% list_rbind(), by = "gene", suffix = c(".grouper",".goby"))->common_all
  
  tibble(genes=common_all %>% inner_join(clown_orth_net$connectivity, by = "gene") %>% filter(module==mod)  %>% pull(gene)) %>% 
    mutate(mod=mod)%>% return()
  }

cols<-homologous_filtered %>% distinct(col.clown)
purrr::map(cols$col.clown, homologous_gene_list) %>% list_rbind() %>% distinct(genes, .keep_all = T)->homologous_genes
homologous_genes %>% distinct(mod)

homologous_genes %>% saveRDS("./RDS/homologous_genes.rds")

#Non-homologus, low preservation modules
clown_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(!module %in% (homologous_genes %>% distinct(mod) %>% pull(mod))) %>% distinct(module)->non_homologous_mods

homologous_modules %>% filter(col.clown %in% non_homologous_mods$module) %>% pivot_longer(contains("col"), names_to = "species.col", values_to = "col") %>% 
  pivot_longer(contains("jaccard"), names_to = "jaccard.comp", values_to = "jaccard.val") %>% 
  pivot_longer(contains("pres"),names_to = "pres.comp", values_to = "pres.val")->homologous_long_non_homologus

#filter out the top 30% non-homologous module comparisons
homologous_long_non_homologus %>% filter(jaccard.val >= quantile(homologous_long_non_homologus$jaccard.val,0.70)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(species.col, col) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = species.col, values_from =
                                                    col) %>% 
  unnest(cols = c(col.goby, col.danio, col.manini, col.grouper, col.clown)) %>%
  distinct(col.goby, col.danio, col.manini, col.grouper, col.clown)->non_homologous_filtered

cols<-non_homologous_filtered %>% distinct(col.clown)
purrr::map(cols$col.clown, homologous_gene_list) %>% list_rbind() %>% distinct(genes, .keep_all = T)->non_homologous_genes
non_homologous_genes %>% distinct(mod)

non_homologous_genes %>% saveRDS("./RDS/non_homologous_genes.rds")
```

### Average connectivity of homologus genes
The homologous genes on an average have higher connectivity than the other genes. Therefore, they represent hub genes.
```{r}
homologous_genes<-readRDS("./RDS/homologous_genes.rds")
#homologous_genes50<-readRDS("./RDS/homologous_genes_50.rds")
#homologous_genes20<-readRDS("./RDS/homologous_genes_20.rds")


#non_homologous_genes<-readRDS("./RDS/non_homologous_genes.rds")
rbind(
  clown_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% 
    mutate(type="Yes"),
  clown_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(!gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% 
    mutate(type="No ")) %>% mutate(sp="Clownfish") %>% 
  rbind(
    rbind(
      grouper_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% 
        mutate(type="Yes"),
      grouper_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(!gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% 
        mutate(type="No")) %>% mutate(sp="Grouper")) %>% 
  rbind(
    rbind(
      goby_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% 
        mutate(type="Yes"),
      goby_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(!gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% 
        mutate(type="No")) %>% mutate(sp="Goby")) %>% 
  rbind(
    rbind(
      manini_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% 
        mutate(type="Yes"),
      manini_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(!gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% 
        mutate(type="No")) %>% mutate(sp="Manini")) %>% 
  rbind(
    rbind(
      danio_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% 
        mutate(type="Yes"),
      danio_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(!gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% 
        mutate(type="No")) %>% mutate(sp="Zebrafish")) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(y=log2(degree),x=type))+
  facet_wrap(~sp, scales="free_x", nrow=1)+
  geom_quasirandom(shape=21, alpha=0.5, color="white", fill="grey40")+
  geom_boxplot(alpha=0.3, fill="grey40", outliers = FALSE, width=0.3)+
  labs(x="In homologous network",
       y="Connectivity")+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill="grey96"))


wil_test_boot<-function(dat,species){
  rbind(
    dat$connectivity %>% filter(gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% mutate(type="homologous"),
    dat$connectivity %>% filter(!gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% mutate(type="other") %>% 
      slice_sample(n = 25)
  )->test_dat
  
  
  tibble(p.value=(
    wilcox.test(
      x = test_dat %>% filter(type=="homologous") %>% pull(degree),
      y = test_dat %>% filter(type=="other") %>% pull(degree),
      alternative = "greater")
    )$p.value,
         sp=paste0(species)
  ) %>% return()
}

rbind(
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = clown_orth_net, species = "Clownfish")) %>% 
  list_rbind(),
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = grouper_orth_net, species = "Grouper")) %>% 
  list_rbind(),
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = goby_orth_net, species = "Goby")) %>%
  list_rbind(),
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = manini_orth_net, species = "Manini")) %>% 
  list_rbind(),
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = danio_orth_net, species = "zebrafish")) %>% 
  list_rbind()
)->all_fish_wil_test_res

all_fish_wil_test_res %>% 
  mutate(p.adj=p.adjust(all_fish_wil_test_res$p.value, method = "BH"))


```

### Gene copy-number of homologous genes
Homologous genes are not comprised of gene families that vary copy-number as compared to the full ortholog set. Suggesting that the developmental network likely does not have more redundancy (purely from a genetic perspective) xthan other sets of gene networks. 
```{r}
rbind(
  orth %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::count(Orthogroup) %>% mutate(type="Homologous"),
  orth %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% full_orths$Orthogroup & !Orthogroup %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% 
    dplyr::count(Orthogroup)  %>% slice_sample(n=2000) %>% mutate(type="Non-homologous"))->ss_test

wilcox.test(x = ss_test %>% 
              filter(type=="Homologous") %>% pull(n) %>% log2(),
            
            y = ss_test %>% 
              filter(type=="Non-homologous") %>% 
              pull(n) %>% log2(), alternative = "two.sided")

ss_test %>%  ggplot(aes(y=log2(n), x=type, fill = type))+
  ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(shape=21)+
  geom_boxplot(color="black", alpha=0.5, outliers = FALSE)+
  theme_bw()+  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#EA5B15","#1AAEC0"))+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
```

```{r, eval=F}
library(GOSemSim)
library(org.Dr.eg.db)
library(AnnotationDbi)

#Load Danio data
read_csv("./03.Annotations/Danio_biomart.csv")->Danio_biomart
#Get GO data
go_annotations <- select(org.Dr.eg.db,
                         keys = keys(org.Dr.eg.db, keytype = "ENSEMBL"), 
                         columns = c("GO", "ONTOLOGY"), 
                         keytype = "ENSEMBL")

#Prepare the semantic data
drGO_BP<-godata('org.Dr.eg.db', keytype="ENSEMBL", ont="BP")
drGO_MF<-godata('org.Dr.eg.db', keytype="ENSEMBL", ont="MF")

#Specify gene sets
geneset_non_homo<-orth %>% filter(sp=="Danio_rerio") %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% full_orths$Orthogroup & !Orthogroup %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% mutate(orths= str_remove(orths,"\\.[0-9]*"))

#Retrieve annotations

go_annotations_MF <- go_annotations %>% filter(ONTOLOGY=="MF")
```

### SS Dendrogram

In this section I do a semantic similarity analysis between GO terms and then make a dendrogram to visualise their diversity and similarity.
```{r,eval=F}
##Compute SS between terms
SemSim_compute<-function(ensembl,annot,measure, semData){
    expand_grid(c1=annot %>% filter(ENSEMBL==paste0(ensembl)) %>% pull(GO),
                c2=annot %>% filter(ENSEMBL==paste0(ensembl)) %>% pull(GO)) %>% 
      filter(c1 != c2) %>% 
  #Ensure symmetric rows are removed
      rowwise() %>%
      mutate(pair = list(sort(c(c1, c2)))) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      distinct(pair, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
      dplyr::select(-pair)->dat
    
    #Make the function to calculate semantic similarity
    avg_semsim<-function(go1,go2,measure,combine,ensembl){
      goSim(go1, go2, semData=semData, measure=measure)->res
      
      data.frame(GO1=go1,
                 GO2=go2,
                 ss=res,
                 ensembl_id=ensembl)->res_dat
      return(res_dat)
      }
    
    purrr::pmap(list(.x = as.list(dat$c1),
                     .y = as.list(dat$c2)), 
                ~avg_semsim(go1=.x, go2=.y, 
                            ensembl=ensembl, 
                            measure = measure)) %>% list_rbind()->ss_res
    return(ss_res)
}

  # Function to get GO term descriptions
  get_go_description <- function(go_terms) {
    library(GO.db)
    map_chr(go_terms, ~ AnnotationDbi::select(GO.db, keys = .x, columns = "TERM", keytype = "GOID")$TERM[1] %||% NA)
  }
  
  
SemSim_compute_module<-function(mod)
  {
  #To get the graphs for the other categories, replace go_annotations_BP, and drGO_BP
  #Prepare the data that has ensembl ids in each module and the filtered enriched GO tems for that module.
  inner_join(go_annotations_BP,
             danio_homo_mods_proc[[mod]]$result %>% filter(FDR < 0.001) %>% dplyr::select(GOBPID),
             by = c("GO"="GOBPID"))->input_GO
  
  purrr::map(.x=as.list(input_GO$ENSEMBL),
             ~SemSim_compute(ensembl = .x, 
                             annot=input_GO, 
                             semData=drGO_BP, measure="Wang")) %>% list_rbind()->ss_out_conv
 quantile(ss_out_conv$ss, 0.75)->qnt
  
  # Add descriptions to dataframe
 df <- ss_out_conv %>% na.omit() %>% filter(ss >= qnt)
 df %>%  saveRDS(paste0("03.Annotations/",mod,"_SS_graph_data_BP.rds"))
 
 library(enrichplot)
 library(clusterProfiler)

# Make custom enrichResult object
 data.frame(ID=c(df$GO1,df$GO2)) %>% mutate(Description=get_go_description(c(df$GO1,df$GO2)))->t
 inner_join(t,df %>% dplyr::select(GO1,ensembl_id) %>% 
              dplyr::rename("ID"="GO1"), by = "ID",relationship = "many-to-many") %>% 
   distinct(ID,ensembl_id, .keep_all = T)->t
 t %>% group_by(ID, Description) %>% mutate(Count=n_distinct(ensembl_id)) %>% ungroup()->t
 t %>% mutate(pvalue=0.05, p.adjust = 0.05) %>% dplyr::rename("geneID"="ensembl_id")->t2
 t2 %>% distinct(ID, .keep_all = T) %>% column_to_rownames("ID") %>%
   mutate(ID=t2 %>% distinct(ID) %>% pull(ID)) %>% 
   dplyr::select(ID, Description, pvalue,p.adjust,geneID,Count)->t2
 
 custom_enrich <- new(
   "enrichResult",
   result = t2 %>% distinct(ID, .keep_all = T),
   organism = "custom",
   keytype = "ENSEMBL",
   ontology = "BP",#Can be kept the same
   gene = unlist(strsplit(t2$geneID, "/")),
   geneSets = list(),
   pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
   pAdjustMethod = "BH")
 
 go_db <- godata('org.Dr.eg.db', ont="BP", computeIC=FALSE)#Change ont for other categories
 sim_matrix <- setReadable(custom_enrich, 'org.Dr.eg.db', 'ENSEMBL')
 sim_matrix <- enrichplot::pairwise_termsim(custom_enrich, semData=go_db, method = "Wang")
 p_sim_matrix<- enrichplot::treeplot(sim_matrix)
 
 dist_matrix <- as.dist(1 - sim_matrix@termsim) 
 hc <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = "complete")
 hc_dendro<-as.dendrogram(hc)
 hc_dendro_data <- ggdendro::dendro_data(hc_dendro,type="rectangle")
 labels_df <- hc_dendro_data$labels
 
 library(ggdendro)
 ggplot(segment(hc_dendro_data)) +
   geom_segment(aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend))+
   geom_text(data = labels_df, 
             aes(x=x, y=y, label=label),
             hjust = 0,vjust = 0.4, size=3)+
   coord_flip()+
   scale_y_reverse(expand = c(0.9, 0))+
   ggsci::scale_color_npg()+
   theme_void() +
   ggtitle(paste0("BP GOterm clustering dendrogram of ",mod," module"))->dendro_plot
 
 return(dendro_plot)

 }
```

## Phylogenomics

In this section I use phylogenetic comparative methods to test for a relationship between changes in copy number between the acanthomorpha radiation and clades predating the radiation. Gene duplication has implication towards the evolution of novelty through processes like neo and subfunctionlisation. Here we test whether there are significant differences in gene copy number of the metamorphosis modules between acanthomorpha and the other clades. We can then study the genes with significant differences to infer how the could contribute to the radiation.\
I first use Pagel's lambda and Bloomberg's K to identify which genes have a significant phylogenetic signal for both measures. Following this, I perform a phylogenetic anova between the acanthomorpha and the other fishes to identify genes that significantly differ in copy number between the two. Before running the phylogenetic anova I remove the lineages that have experiences an additional whole genome duplication. Since these lineages are outside acanthomorpha they would inflate the difference in gene copy without necessarily being related to the species radiation.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
##Tree used for phyloANOVA
left_join(taxa %>% filter(!Family %in% c("Cyprinidae","Cobitidae","Catostomidae","Salmonidae")), 
          tibble(sp=pruned_tree$tip.label),by = "sp")->tips_to_keep
drop.tip(pruned_tree,pruned_tree$tip.label[-match(tips_to_keep$sp, pruned_tree$tip.label)])->no_WGD_tree

#Acanthomorpha
##Non-homologous module
non_homologous_genes<-readRDS("./RDS/non_homologous_genes.rds")
non_homologous_genes %>% distinct(mod) %>% pull(mod)->cols
purrr::map(.x=cols,
```

## CAFE Analysis

I use the birth-and-death model implemented in CAFE5 to further validate the difference in gene copy number observed between acanthomorpha and non-acanthomorpha fishes. I run a base model with a uniform lambda for the entire tree and compare the model fit with a multilamda model where gene familes in acanthomorpha and non-acanthomorpha evolve at different rates.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
non_homologous_genes<-readRDS("./RDS/non_homologous_genes.rds")
homologous_genes<-readRDS("./RDS/homologous_genes.rds")

#random_non_homologus_genes<-clown_orth_net$connectivity %>% 
#  filter(!gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% 
#    slice_sample(n = 1196) %>% dplyr::rename("genes"="gene","mod"="module")#Random gene set to test specificity of CAFE

#random_non_homologus_genes<-random_non_homologus_genes3

#Make CAFE input
make_cafe_input<-function(genelist, cols){
  specific_module<-genelist %>% filter(mod==cols)
  
  orth_gene_copy %>% filter(sp %in% no_WGD_tree$tip.label) %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% specific_module$genes) %>%
    dplyr::select(-c(Family, Order, SpecCode)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = sp, values_from = no_of_gene_copies) %>%
    replace(is.na(.), 0) %>% mutate(`Family ID`=paste0("OG",Orthogroup), Desc="(null)") %>% 
    dplyr::select(c(Desc, `Family ID`, everything(), -Orthogroup)) %>% 
    write_tsv(paste0("./06.CAFE5/New_results/cafe_input_",cols,".tsv"))#change destination in needed
}


non_homologous_genes %>% distinct(mod) %>% pull(mod)->cols
purrr::map(.x = cols, 
           ~make_cafe_input(genelist = non_homologous_genes, cols = .x))

homologous_genes %>% distinct(mod) %>% pull(mod)->cols
purrr::map(.x = cols, 
           ~make_cafe_input(genelist = homologous_genes, cols = .x))

random_non_homologus_genes %>% distinct(mod) %>% pull(mod)->cols
purrr::map(.x = cols, 
           ~make_cafe_input(genelist = random_non_homologus_genes, cols = .x))

```

```{r}
get_cafe_family_results<-function(cols){
  read_table(paste0("./06.CAFE5/New_results/results_cafe_",cols,"/Multi_lambda_model_1/Base_family_results.txt"),
             skip = 1, col_names= c("genes","pval","is_sig"))->fam
  
  fam %>% mutate(mod=cols,
                 genes=str_remove_all(genes,"OG")) %>% return()
}

get_cafe_model_outputs<-function(cols){
  read_table(paste0("./06.CAFE5/New_results/results_cafe_",cols,"/Base_model/Base_results.txt"),col_names = c("q","w","e","r","t","y"))->b
  
  tibble("neglogL"=b$y[1],
         "lambda1"=b$w[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "lambda2"=b$e[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "model_type"="base")->base_model
  
  read_table(paste0("./06.CAFE5/New_results/results_cafe_",cols,"/Multi_lambda_model_1/Base_results.txt"),
             col_names=c("q","w","e","r","t","y"))->m1
  
  tibble("neglogL"=m1$y[1],
       "lambda1"=m1$w[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "lambda2"=m1$e[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "model_type"="multi_lambda_1")->multi_1
  
  read_table(paste0("./06.CAFE5/New_results/results_cafe_",cols,"/Multi_lambda_model_2/Base_results.txt"),
             col_names=c("q","w","e","r","t","y"))->m2
  
  tibble("neglogL"=m2$y[1],
         "lambda1"=m2$w[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "lambda2"=m2$e[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "model_type"="multi_lambda_2")->multi_2
  
  read_table(paste0("./06.CAFE5/New_results/results_cafe_",cols,"/Multi_lambda_model_3/Base_results.txt"),
           col_names=c("q","w","e","r","t","y"))->m3
  
  tibble("neglogL"=m3$y[1],
         "lambda1"=m3$w[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "lambda2"=m3$e[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "model_type"="multi_lambda_3")->multi_3
  
 rbind(base_model, multi_1, multi_2, multi_3) %>% mutate(mod=cols) %>% 
    replace(is.na(.), 0) %>% return()

}
```

```{r}
wil_test_boot<-function(dat,species){
  rbind(
    dat$connectivity %>% filter(gene %in% (cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(is_sig=="y") %>% pull(genes))) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% mutate(type="homologous"),
    dat$connectivity %>% filter(gene %in% homologous_genes$genes & !gene %in% (cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(is_sig=="y") %>% pull(genes))) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% mutate(type="other") %>% 
      slice_sample(n=167)
  )->test_dat
  
  
  tibble(p.value=(
    wilcox.test(
      x = test_dat %>% filter(type=="homologous") %>% pull(degree),
      y = test_dat %>% filter(type=="other") %>% pull(degree),
      alternative = "two.sided")
    )$p.value,
         sp=paste0(species)
  ) %>% return()
}

rbind(

  list_rbind(),
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = goby_orth_net, species = "Goby")) %>%

purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = manini_orth_net, species = "Manini")) %>%

purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = danio_orth_net, species = "zebrafish")) %>%
```

#### Plotting CAFE results

##### Model fit

The plot below shows the negative log-likelihoods for two models implemented in CAFE. The Base model, with a single rate acorss the entire tree, and a multi-lambda model where the acanthomorpha and non-acanthomorpha fish have different rates. For all of the homologous modules, except royalblue, the multi-lambda model is a better fit to the data.

```{r}

  facet_wrap(~mod, scales="free_y")+
  geom_point(shape=21, color="grey20", size=3)+

  labs(title = "CAFE5 model outputs")+
  theme_linedraw()+

         strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#67980C"))
```

##### Expansion and contraction of gene families

Here we plot the relative expansion and contraction of homologous gene families estimated by CAFE. We see that there are different points of expansion/contraction along the tree occurring at different nodes. The highest expansion occurred at the root of teleost as a result of the teleost specific whole genome duplication (3R). The second point of expansion appears at the branch leading to *Danio rerio*. This is signal is likely due to the fact that *Danio rerio* has a large proportion of retained ohnologs from the 3R.\
The expansions and contractions are all significant.

###### Proportion of Ohnologs

Here I look for the proportion of ohnologs in the fast evolving genes estimated from cafe. I use the ohnolog list form zebrafish (<http://ohnologs.curie.fr/>) to cross-reference the zebrafish orthologs in my data and estimate the proportions. I see that a majority (74%) of the genes are not classified as ohnologs. When looking at each module, we see some are comprised of a mix of ohnologs and non-ohnologs, while many contain only non-ohnologs. The cyan module comprises entirely of ohnologs. When looking at the time of duplication I see that a majority of the ohnologs were duplicated during the teleost whole genome duplication.

###### At the tips

Focusing on the changes taking place in the branches leading up to the tips, we observed different degrees of expansion and contraction. At the species level, *Danio rerio* displayed the highest degree of expansion likely due to the high retention of 3R ohnologs. There were species that had only expansion and contractions.\
At the Order level, Perciformes and Syngnathiformes had the highest degrees of expansion/contraction.

## PGLMM

In this section I take the rapidly evolving genes estimated from cafe and check whether there is any relationship between copy number, phenotypic traits, and ecological traits. For this I use a phylogenetic generalised linear mixed model implemented in brms.\
Since there are multiple genes in each module, and multiple trait measurements, I use phylogenetic PCA scores and estimate correlations between the first two PC of the trait matrix and the first two PC axes of the gene count matrix. I model the PCs of the trait as a multivariate response variable essentially allowing me to test for relationships between composite traits, like morphology (length, fish depth, fish width) and swimming performance (caudal depth and caudal width).

### Relationships between PC axes

Before running the model I need to know which genes and which traits have a relationship worth exploring. To get the list of genes and traits I simply perform the PCA and plot the PC scores followed by a spearman correlation test (not corrected for phylogeny). I then pick the ones that show some possibility of a relationship, usually with a rho \>=0.1 and P \<= 0.05.\
The plots can be viewed below.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#Plots for spearman correlation between components
cafe_cols<-cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(is_sig=="y") %>% janitor::get_dupes(mod) %>% distinct(mod) %>% pull(mod)
purrr::map(cafe_cols,gene_copy_comp_trait_comp)->trait_gene_components_plots
names(trait_gene_components_plots)<-cafe_cols  
```

```{r}
trait_gene_components_plots<-readRDS("./05.Phylogenomics/trait_gene_components_plots.rds")
```

### Data from fish shapes model

```{r}
#Get shapes data
shapes_dat<-read_csv("./05.Phylogenomics/FishShapes/doi_10_5061_dryad_vt4b8gtvf__v20220614/FishShapes_specimensv1.csv") %>% drop_na()

shapes_dat %>% filter(Tree_name %in% no_WGD_tree$tip.label) %>% group_by(Tree_name) %>%
  mutate(total_weight=mean(Total_weight), 
         length=mean(Standard_length), 
         body_depth=mean(Max_body_depth),
         fish_width=mean(Max_fish_width),
         head_depth=mean(Head_depth),
         lower_jaw_length=mean(Lower_jaw_length),
         mounth_width=mean(Mouth_width),
         min_caudalpeduncle_depth=mean(Min_caudalpeduncle_depth),
         min_caudalpeduncle_width=mean(Min_caudalpeduncle_width)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::select(Tree_name,Family, Order, total_weight, length, body_depth, fish_width,head_depth, lower_jaw_length, mounth_width,
                min_caudalpeduncle_depth, min_caudalpeduncle_width) %>% dplyr::rename("sp"="Tree_name") %>% distinct(sp, .keep_all = T)->shapes_dat

#Prune the no_WGD_tree
pglmm_tree<-drop.tip(no_WGD_tree,no_WGD_tree$tip.label[-match(shapes_dat$sp, no_WGD_tree$tip.label)])
is.rooted(pglmm_tree)
is.ultrametric(pglmm_tree)


#ecological data
ecology %>% filter(sp %in% shapes_dat$sp) %>% distinct(sp, .keep_all = T) %>% dplyr::select(sp, Family, Order, Neritic, Intertidal, Epipelagic, Estuaries, Mangroves, Oceanic, Herbivory2, FeedingType) %>% replace_na(list(Herbivory2="not_available", FeedingType="not_available"))->ecology_data

brms_model<-function(col,dat){

orth_gene_copy %>%
    filter(Orthogroup %in% (cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(mod==col) %>% pull(genes))) %>% 
  filter(sp %in% pglmm_tree$tip.label) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(Family, Order, SpecCode)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Orthogroup, values_from = no_of_gene_copies) %>% 
  replace(is.na(.), 0) %>% filter(sp %in% shapes_dat$sp)->sp_genes_wide
colnames(sp_genes_wide)<-c("sp", paste0("gene",seq(1:(ncol(sp_genes_wide)-1))))

#genes pPCA
expr_scaled<-sp_genes_wide %>% column_to_rownames("sp")->pca_dat_gene
scale(pca_dat_gene,center = FALSE,scale = TRUE)->pca_dat_gene
pca_gene <- phyl.pca(pglmm_tree, pca_dat_gene, method = "lambda", mode = "corr")
pca_gene <- as.data.frame(pca_gene$S) %>% dplyr::rename_with(~paste0(.,".cpy")) %>% 
  rownames_to_column("sp")

#traits pPCA
dat %>% column_to_rownames("sp")->pca_dat
scale(pca_dat,center = FALSE,scale = TRUE)->pca_dat
pca_res <- phyl.pca(pglmm_tree, pca_dat, method = "lambda", mode = "corr")
pca_shapes <- as.data.frame(pca_res$S) %>% dplyr::rename_with(~paste0(.,".trait")) %>% 
  rownames_to_column("sp")

#model dat
left_join(pca_gene,pca_shapes)->model_dat

model_dat %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=PC1.trait))+geom_density()

is.rooted(no_WGD_tree)
is.ultrametric(no_WGD_tree)

#Set default priors
library(brms)
A<-MCMCglmm::inverseA(pglmm_tree,scale = TRUE, nodes = "TIPS")#covariance structure for species
A<-A$Ainv

priors<-get_prior(mvbind(PC1.trait,PC2.trait) ~  PC1.cpy  + PC2.cpy + (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
                  data = model_dat,
                  data2   = list(A = A),
                  family = skew_normal())

#model
model_brms_out <- brm(
  mvbind(PC1.trait,PC2.trait) ~  PC1.cpy  + PC2.cpy + (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),
  data = model_dat,
  data2   = list(A = A),
  prior = priors,
  family = skew_normal(),
  chains = 4, 
  cores = 4,
  iter = 4000, 
  warmup = 1000,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  control = list(adapt_delta=0.999, max_treedepth = 12)
)


return(model_brms_out)
}

```

#### Run the models

```{r}
purrr::map(.x=cafe_cols,
           ~brms_model(col = .x,
           dat = shapes_dat %>% dplyr::select(sp, min_caudalpeduncle_depth, min_caudalpeduncle_width)))->model_brms_caudalpeduncle
names(model_brms_caudalpeduncle)<-cafe_cols
model_brms_caudalpeduncle %>% saveRDS("./RDS/model_brms_caudalpeduncle.rds")

purrr::map(.x=cafe_cols,
           ~brms_model(col = .x,
           dat = shapes_dat %>% dplyr::select(sp,length,body_depth,fish_width)))->model_brms_body
names(model_brms_body)<-cafe_cols
model_brms_body %>% saveRDS("./RDS/model_brms_body.rds")

purrr::map(.x=cafe_cols,
           ~brms_model(col = .x,
           dat = shapes_dat %>% dplyr::select(sp,head_depth,lower_jaw_length,mounth_width)))->model_brms_head
names(model_brms_head)<-cafe_cols
model_brms_head %>% saveRDS("./RDS/model_brms_head.rds")
```

```{r}
scale(pca_dat,center = FALSE,scale = TRUE)->pca_dat
pca_res <- phyl.pca(pglmm_tree, pca_dat, method = "lambda", mode = "corr")
pca_shapes <- as.data.frame(pca_res$S) %>% dplyr::rename_with(~paste0(.,".trait")) %>% 
  rownames_to_column("sp")

#model dat
left_join(pca_gene,pca_shapes)->model_dat

model_dat %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=PC1.trait))+geom_density()

is.rooted(no_WGD_tree)
is.ultrametric(no_WGD_tree)

#Set default priors
library(brms)
A<-MCMCglmm::inverseA(pglmm_tree,scale = TRUE, nodes = "TIPS")#covariance structure for species
A<-A$Ainv

priors<-get_prior(mvbind(PC1.trait,PC2.trait) ~  PC1.cpy  + PC2.cpy + (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
                  data = model_dat,
                  data2   = list(A = A),
                  family = skew_normal())

#model
model_brms_out <- brm(
  mvbind(PC1.trait,PC2.trait) ~  PC1.cpy  + PC2.cpy + (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),
  data = model_dat,
  data2   = list(A = A),
  prior = priors,
  family = skew_normal(),
  chains = 4, 
  cores = 4,
  iter = 4000, 
  warmup = 1000,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  control = list(adapt_delta=0.999, max_treedepth = 12)
)


return(model_brms_out)
}

brms_model_random(dat = shapes_dat %>% dplyr::select(sp,head_depth,lower_jaw_length,mounth_width))->model_brms_head_random1
```

### Data from FishBase

Here I use data from FishBase to check for a relationship between the gene copy PC axes and ecological feature such as habitat zone, and type of diet. Since the features here are binary categories, I run a different type of model compared to the above one for the shapes data.\
Here I model the first two PC axes of the gene copy matrix as a multivariate response variable with each ecological feature as predictor. The feature levels here are a binary classification of 0 and -1. Similar to the mode for shapes I use a skewed gaussian distribution to model the gene PC axes.\
This model essentially checks whether ecological features can predict the position of fish species on the gene copy number PC space.

```{r}
brms_model_ecology<-function(col){
  library(brms)
#lead the genecopy data
  cafe_genefamily_outs<-cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(is_sig=="y")
orth_gene_copy %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% (cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(mod==col) %>% 
                                             pull(genes))) %>% 
  filter(sp %in% pglmm_tree$tip.label) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(Family, Order, SpecCode)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Orthogroup, values_from = no_of_gene_copies) %>% 
  replace(is.na(.), 0) %>% filter(sp %in% shapes_dat$sp)->sp_genes_wide
#colnames(sp_genes_wide)<-c("sp", paste0("gene",seq(1:(ncol(sp_genes_wide)-1))))

expr_scaled<-sp_genes_wide %>% column_to_rownames("sp")->pca_dat_gene
scale(pca_dat_gene, center = FALSE,scale = TRUE)->pca_dat_gene
pca_gene_pca <- phyl.pca(pglmm_tree, pca_dat_gene, method = "lambda", mode = "corr")
pca_gene <- as.data.frame(pca_gene_pca$S) %>% dplyr::rename_with(~paste0(.,".cpy")) %>% 
  rownames_to_column("sp")

#modify the ecology data from fishbase to only select informative features and keep species in genes data and tree
ecology %>% dplyr::select(sp, Family, Order, SpecCode, Neritic, Oceanic, Intertidal, Epipelagic, Mangroves,
                          Herbivory2, FeedingType) %>% 
  replace_na(list(Herbivory2="not_available",FeedingType="not_available")) %>% 
  filter(sp %in% pglmm_tree$tip.label) %>% distinct(sp, .keep_all = T) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(Family,Order,SpecCode))->ecology_model

ecology_model %>% 
  mutate(Neritic=as.factor(ecology_model$Neritic),
         Oceanic=as.factor(ecology_model$Oceanic),
         Intertidal=as.factor(ecology_model$Intertidal),
         Epipelagic=as.factor(ecology_model$Epipelagic),
         Mangroves=as.factor(ecology_model$Mangroves),
         Herbivory2=as.factor(ecology_model$Herbivory2),
         FeedingType=as.factor(ecology_model$FeedingType))->ecology_model


left_join(pca_gene,ecology_model) %>% drop_na() %>% filter(FeedingType != "not_available")->model_dat

#Prune the pglmm tree
pglmm_tree_fishbase<-drop.tip(pglmm_tree,pglmm_tree$tip.label[-match(model_dat$sp, pglmm_tree$tip.label)])
is.rooted(pglmm_tree_fishbase)
is.ultrametric(pglmm_tree_fishbase)
#Must pass namecheck
geiger::name.check(pglmm_tree_fishbase,model_dat %>% column_to_rownames("sp"))


#plots to visualise response and predictors
ggarrange(
model_dat %>% pivot_longer(c(Neritic,Oceanic,Intertidal,Epipelagic,Mangroves), names_to = "zone") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(y = PC1.cpy, x= zone))+
  ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(aes(group=as.factor(value), 
                                   fill = as.factor(value),
                                   color = as.factor(value)),
                               shape=21,
                               size=2,
                               dodge.width = 0.8,
                               method = "tukeyDense", 
                               alpha=0.7)+
  geom_boxplot(aes(group=as.factor(value), 
                   colour = as.factor(value)),
               fill="white",
               alpha=0.5,
               outliers = FALSE)+
  facet_wrap(~zone, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1)+
  ggsci::scale_fill_jama()+
  ggsci::scale_color_jama()+
  labs(title = "Gene component scores per zone",
       x = NULL)+
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    strip.text   = element_text()),

model_dat %>% pivot_longer(c(Neritic,Oceanic,Intertidal,Epipelagic,Mangroves), names_to = "zone") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(y = PC2.cpy, x= zone))+
  ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(aes(group=as.factor(value), 
                                   fill = as.factor(value),
                                   color = as.factor(value)),
                               shape=21,
                               size=2,
                               dodge.width = 0.8,
                               method = "tukeyDense", 
                               alpha=0.7)+
  geom_boxplot(aes(group=as.factor(value), 
                   colour = as.factor(value)),
               fill="white",
               alpha=0.5,
               outliers = FALSE)+
  facet_wrap(~zone, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1)+
  ggsci::scale_fill_jama()+
  ggsci::scale_color_jama()+
  labs(x = NULL)+
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    strip.text   = element_text()),
nrow = 2, common.legend = T,legend = "right")->zone_plots
#plots to visualise response and predictors
ggarrange(
  model_dat %>% pivot_longer(c(Herbivory2,FeedingType), names_to = "feed") %>% 
    ggplot(aes(y = PC1.cpy, x= feed))+
    ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(aes(group=as.factor(value), 
                                     fill = as.factor(value),
                                     color = as.factor(value)),
                                 shape=21,
                                 size=2,
                                 dodge.width = 0.8,
                                 method = "tukeyDense", 
                                 alpha=0.7)+
    geom_boxplot(aes(group=as.factor(value), 
                     colour = as.factor(value)),
                 fill="white",
                 alpha=0.5,
                 outliers = FALSE)+
    facet_wrap(~feed, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1)+
    ggsci::scale_fill_aaas()+
    ggsci::scale_color_aaas()+
    labs(title = "Gene component scores per feed",
         x = NULL)+
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      strip.text   = element_text()),
  
  model_dat %>% pivot_longer(c(Herbivory2,FeedingType), names_to = "feed") %>% 
    ggplot(aes(y = PC2.cpy, x= feed))+
    ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(aes(group=as.factor(value), 
                                     fill = as.factor(value),
                                     color = as.factor(value)),
                                 shape=21,
                                 size=2,
                                 dodge.width = 0.8,
                                 method = "tukeyDense", 
                                 alpha=0.7)+
    geom_boxplot(aes(group=as.factor(value), 
                     colour = as.factor(value)),
                 fill="white",
                 alpha=0.5,
                 outliers = FALSE)+
    facet_wrap(~feed, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1)+
    ggsci::scale_fill_aaas()+
    ggsci::scale_color_aaas()+
    labs(x = NULL)+
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      strip.text   = element_text()),
  nrow = 2, common.legend = T,legend = "right")->feed_plots

#Phylogenetic covariance matrix
A<-MCMCglmm::inverseA(pglmm_tree_fishbase,scale = TRUE,nodes = "TIPS")
A<-A$Ainv
#Priors
priors_zone<-get_prior(mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
                    0 + Neritic  + Oceanic + Intertidal + Epipelagic + Mangroves +(1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
                  data = model_dat,
                  data2   = list(A = A),
                  family = skew_normal())
#Model
model_brms_zone <- brm(
  mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
    0 + Neritic  + Oceanic + Intertidal + Epipelagic + Mangroves +(1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),
  data = model_dat,
  data2   = list(A = A),
  prior = priors_zone,
  family = skew_normal(),
  chains = 4, 
  cores = 4,
  iter = 4000, 
  warmup = 1000,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  control = list(adapt_delta=0.999, max_treedepth = 12)
)


priors_feed<-get_prior(mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
                         0 + Herbivory2  + FeedingType + (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
                       data = model_dat,
                       data2   = list(A = A),
                       family = skew_normal())

#model
model_brms_feed <- brm(
  mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
    0 + Herbivory2  + FeedingType + (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),
  data = model_dat,
  data2   = list(A = A),
  prior = priors_feed,
  family = skew_normal(),
  chains = 4, 
  cores = 4,
  iter = 4000, 
  warmup = 1000,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  control = list(adapt_delta=0.999, max_treedepth = 12)
)

return(list(pca_gene_pca=pca_gene_pca,
            zone_plots=zone_plots,
            feed_plots=feed_plots,
            model_brms_zone=model_brms_zone,
            model_brms_feed=model_brms_feed))
}
brms_model_brain<-function(col){
    library(brms)

#lead the genecopy data
orth_gene_copy %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% (cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(mod==col) %>% 
                                             pull(genes))) %>% 
  filter(sp %in% pglmm_tree$tip.label) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(Family, Order, SpecCode)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Orthogroup, values_from = no_of_gene_copies) %>% 
  replace(is.na(.), 0) %>% filter(sp %in% shapes_dat$sp)->sp_genes_wide
#colnames(sp_genes_wide)<-c("sp", paste0("gene",seq(1:(ncol(sp_genes_wide)-1))))

expr_scaled<-sp_genes_wide %>% column_to_rownames("sp")->pca_dat_gene
scale(pca_dat_gene, center = FALSE,scale = TRUE)->pca_dat_gene
pca_gene_pca <- phyl.pca(pglmm_tree, pca_dat_gene, method = "lambda", mode = "corr")
pca_gene <- as.data.frame(pca_gene_pca$S) %>% dplyr::rename_with(~paste0(.,".cpy")) %>% 
  rownames_to_column("sp")

#modify the ecology data from fishbase to only select informative features and keep species in genes data and tree
brain %>% dplyr::select(sp, BrainWeight) %>% 
  drop_na() %>% summarise(BrainWeight=mean(BrainWeight), .by = sp) %>% 
  filter(sp %in% pglmm_tree$tip.label) %>% distinct(sp, .keep_all = T) %>% column_to_rownames("sp") %>% 
  log2() %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% rownames_to_column("sp")->brain_model

left_join(pca_gene,brain_model) %>% drop_na()->model_dat

#Prune the pglmm tree
pglmm_tree_fishbase<-drop.tip(pglmm_tree,pglmm_tree$tip.label[-match(model_dat$sp, pglmm_tree$tip.label)])
is.rooted(pglmm_tree_fishbase)
is.ultrametric(pglmm_tree_fishbase)
#Must pass namecheck
geiger::name.check(pglmm_tree_fishbase,model_dat %>% column_to_rownames("sp"))

#model_dat %>% ggplot(aes(x=PC1.cpy))+geom_density()

#plots to visualise response and predictors
ggarrange(
  model_dat %>% 
    ggplot(aes(y=PC1.cpy, x=BrainWeight))+
    geom_point(shape=21, fill="#8BAE06", size=3)+
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE,colour = "#F0710F")+
    theme_linedraw(),
  
  model_dat %>% 
    ggplot(aes(y=PC2.cpy, x=BrainWeight))+
    geom_point(shape=21, fill="#8BAE06", size=3)+
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE,colour = "#F0710F")+
    theme_linedraw(),
  nrow = 1, ncol = 2)->brain_plots

#Phylogenetic covariance matrix
A<-MCMCglmm::inverseA(pglmm_tree_fishbase,scale = TRUE,nodes = "TIPS")
A<-A$Ainv
#Priors
priors_brain<-get_prior(mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
                         BrainWeight +(1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
                  data = model_dat,
                  data2   = list(A = A),
                  family = skew_normal())
#Model
model_brms_brain <- brm(
  mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
    BrainWeight +(1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),
  data = model_dat,
  data2   = list(A = A),
  prior = priors_brain,
  family = skew_normal(),
  chains = 4, 
  cores = 4,
  iter = 5000, 
  warmup = 1000,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  control = list(adapt_delta=0.999, max_treedepth = 12)
)


return(list(pca_gene_pca=pca_gene_pca,
            brain_plots=brain_plots,
            model_brms_brain=model_brms_brain))
}

brms_model_repro<-function(col){
    library(brms)

#lead the genecopy data
orth_gene_copy %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% (cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(mod==col) %>% 
                                             pull(genes))) %>% 
  filter(sp %in% pglmm_tree$tip.label) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(Family, Order, SpecCode)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Orthogroup, values_from = no_of_gene_copies) %>% 
  replace(is.na(.), 0) %>% filter(sp %in% shapes_dat$sp)->sp_genes_wide
#colnames(sp_genes_wide)<-c("sp", paste0("gene",seq(1:(ncol(sp_genes_wide)-1))))

expr_scaled<-sp_genes_wide %>% column_to_rownames("sp")->pca_dat_gene
scale(pca_dat_gene, center = FALSE,scale = TRUE)->pca_dat_gene
pca_gene_pca <- phyl.pca(pglmm_tree, pca_dat_gene, method = "lambda", mode = "corr")
pca_gene <- as.data.frame(pca_gene_pca$S) %>% dplyr::rename_with(~paste0(.,".cpy")) %>% 
  rownames_to_column("sp")

#modify the ecology data from fishbase to only select informative features and keep species in genes data and tree
reproduction %>% dplyr::select(sp, ReproMode, Fertilization, RepGuild1, RepGuild2, ParentalCare) %>%  
  replace_na(list(ReproMode="not available",
                  Fertilization="not available",
                  RepGuild1="not available",
                  RepGuild2="not available",
                  ParentalCare="not available")) %>% 
  filter(sp %in% pglmm_tree$tip.label) %>% distinct(sp, .keep_all = T)->repro_model

left_join(pca_gene,repro_model) %>% 
  replace_na(list(ReproMode="not available",
                  Fertilization="not available",
                  RepGuild1="not available",
                  RepGuild2="not available",
                  ParentalCare="not available"))->model_dat

model_dat %>% mutate(ReproMode=as.factor(model_dat$ReproMode),
                     Fertilization=as.factor(model_dat$Fertilization),
                     RepGuild1=as.factor(model_dat$RepGuild1),
                     RepGuild2=as.factor(model_dat$RepGuild2),
                     ParentalCare=as.factor(model_dat$ParentalCare)) %>% 
  filter(ReproMode != "not available" & 
           Fertilization != "not available" & 
           RepGuild1 != "not available" & 
           RepGuild2 != "not available" & 
           ParentalCare !=  "not available") ->model_dat

#Prune the pglmm tree

#Phylogenetic covariance matrix
A<-MCMCglmm::inverseA(pglmm_tree_fishbase,scale = TRUE,nodes = "TIPS")
A<-A$Ainv


#Priors
priors_repro<-get_prior(mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
                          0 + ReproMode +
                           (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
                  data = model_dat,
                  data2   = list(A = A),
                  family = skew_normal())
#Model
model_brms_repro <- brm(
  mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
    0 + ReproMode + 
   (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
  data = model_dat,
  data2   = list(A = A),
  prior = priors_repro,
  family = skew_normal(),
  chains = 4, 
  cores = 4,
  iter = 4000, 
  warmup = 1000,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  control = list(adapt_delta=0.999, max_treedepth = 12)
)

#Priors
priors_fert<-get_prior(mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
                          0 + Fertilization +
                          (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
                        data = model_dat,
                        data2   = list(A = A),
                        family = skew_normal())
#Model

  mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
    0 + Fertilization + 
    (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
  data = model_dat,
  data2   = list(A = A),
  prior = priors_fert,
  family = skew_normal(),
  chains = 4, 
  cores = 4,
  iter = 4000, 
  warmup = 1000,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  control = list(adapt_delta=0.999, max_treedepth = 12)
)

#Priors
priors_RepGuild1<-get_prior(mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
                              0 + RepGuild1 +
                              (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
                            data = model_dat,
                            data2   = list(A = A),
                            family = skew_normal())
#Model
model_brms_RepGuild1 <- brm(
  mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
    0 + RepGuild1 + 
    (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
  data = model_dat,
  data2   = list(A = A),
  prior = priors_RepGuild1,

#Priors

                         0 + RepGuild2 +
                         (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
                       data = model_dat,
                       data2   = list(A = A),
                       family = skew_normal())
#Model
model_brms_RepGuild2 <- brm(
  mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
    0 + RepGuild2 + 
    (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
  data = model_dat,

  prior = priors_RepGuild2,
  family = skew_normal(),
  chains = 4, 
  cores = 4,
  iter = 4000, 
  warmup = 1000,

  control = list(adapt_delta=0.999, max_treedepth = 12)
)

#Priors
priors_ParentalCare<-get_prior(mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
                              0 + ParentalCare +
                              (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
                            data = model_dat,
                            data2   = list(A = A),
                            family = skew_normal())
#Model
model_brms_ParentalCare <- brm(
  mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~

brms_model_swim<-function(col){
    library(brms)

#lead the genecopy data
orth_gene_copy %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% (cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(mod==col) %>% 
                                             pull(genes))) %>% 
  filter(sp %in% pglmm_tree$tip.label) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(Family, Order, SpecCode)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Orthogroup, values_from = no_of_gene_copies) %>% 
  replace(is.na(.), 0) %>% filter(sp %in% shapes_dat$sp)->sp_genes_wide
#colnames(sp_genes_wide)<-c("sp", paste0("gene",seq(1:(ncol(sp_genes_wide)-1))))

expr_scaled<-sp_genes_wide %>% column_to_rownames("sp")->pca_dat_gene
scale(pca_dat_gene, center = FALSE,scale = TRUE)->pca_dat_gene
pca_gene_pca <- phyl.pca(pglmm_tree, pca_dat_gene, method = "lambda", mode = "corr")
pca_gene <- as.data.frame(pca_gene_pca$S) %>% dplyr::rename_with(~paste0(.,".cpy")) %>% 
  rownames_to_column("sp")

#modify the ecology data from fishbase to only select informative features and keep species in genes data and tree
swimming %>% dplyr::select(sp,AdultMode) %>%  
  replace_na(list(AdultMode="not available")) %>% 
  filter(sp %in% pglmm_tree$tip.label) %>% distinct(sp, .keep_all = T)->swim_model

left_join(pca_gene,swim_model) %>% 
  replace_na(list(AdultMode="not available"))->model_dat

model_dat %>% mutate(AdultMode=as.factor(model_dat$AdultMode)) %>% filter(AdultMode !="not available")->model_dat

#Prune the pglmm tree
pglmm_tree_fishbase<-drop.tip(pglmm_tree,pglmm_tree$tip.label[-match(model_dat$sp, pglmm_tree$tip.label)])
is.rooted(pglmm_tree_fishbase)
is.ultrametric(pglmm_tree_fishbase)
#Must pass namecheck
geiger::name.check(pglmm_tree_fishbase,model_dat %>% column_to_rownames("sp"))

#model_dat %>% ggplot(aes(x=PC1.cpy))+geom_density()

#plots to visualise response and predictors
ggarrange(
  model_dat %>% 
    ggplot(aes(y=PC1.cpy, x=AdultMode))+
    ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(aes(group=as.factor(AdultMode), 
                                     fill = as.factor(AdultMode),
                                     color = as.factor(AdultMode)),
                                 shape=21,
                                 size=2,
                                 dodge.width = 0.8,
                                 method = "tukeyDense", 
                                 alpha=0.7)+
    geom_boxplot(aes(group=as.factor(AdultMode), 
                     colour = as.factor(AdultMode)),
                 fill="white",
                 alpha=0.5,
                 outliers = FALSE)+
    facet_wrap(~AdultMode, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1)+
    ggsci::scale_fill_aaas()+
    ggsci::scale_color_aaas()+
    labs(title = "Gene component scores per place of swimming mode",
         x = NULL)+
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      strip.text   = element_blank()),
  
  model_dat %>% 
    ggplot(aes(y=PC2.cpy, x=AdultMode))+
    ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(aes(group=as.factor(AdultMode), 
                                     fill = as.factor(AdultMode),
                                     color = as.factor(AdultMode)),
                                 shape=21,
                                 size=2,
                                 dodge.width = 0.8,
                                 method = "tukeyDense", 
                                 alpha=0.7)+
    geom_boxplot(aes(group=as.factor(AdultMode), 
                     colour = as.factor(AdultMode)),
                 fill="white",
                 alpha=0.5,
                 outliers = FALSE)+
    facet_wrap(~AdultMode, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1)+
    ggsci::scale_fill_aaas()+
    ggsci::scale_color_aaas()+
    labs(title = NULL,
         x = NULL)+
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      strip.text   = element_blank()),
  nrow = 2, ncol = 1, common.legend = T, legend = "right")->swim_plots


#Phylogenetic covariance matrix
A<-MCMCglmm::inverseA(pglmm_tree_fishbase,scale = TRUE,nodes = "TIPS")
A<-A$Ainv


#Priors
priors_swim<-get_prior(mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
                          0 + AdultMode +
                           (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
                  data = model_dat,
                  data2   = list(A = A),
                  family = skew_normal())
#Model
model_brms_swim <- brm(
  mvbind(PC1.cpy,PC2.cpy) ~  
    0 + AdultMode + 
   (1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
  data = model_dat,
  data2   = list(A = A),
  prior = priors_swim,
  family = skew_normal(),
  chains = 4, 
  cores = 4,
  iter = 4000, 
  warmup = 1000,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  control = list(adapt_delta=0.999, max_treedepth = 12)
)



return(list(pca_gene_pca=pca_gene_pca,
            swim_plots=swim_plots,
            model_brms_swim=model_brms_swim))
}
```

## Phenotypic effect of genes

In this section I check for the phenotypic effects of the rapidly evolving gene families whose variation in copy number if linked to phenotypic trait variation.

```{r}
read_csv("./08.ZFIN/Danio_biomart.csv")->Danio_biomart #Obtained from bioMart package
read_tsv("./08.ZFIN/phenoGeneCleanData_fish_2023.05.07.tsv")->pheno #Download from ZFIN
read_tsv("./08.ZFIN/ensembl_1_to_1_2025.08.26.txt")->zfin_ids #Download from ZFIN
zfin_ids$...5<-NULL


Danio_biomart %>% filter(`Gene stable ID` %in% zfin_ids$Ensembl_ID)

left_join(Danio_biomart, zfin_ids, by=c("Gene stable ID"="Ensembl_ID")) %>% distinct(ZFIN_ID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  left_join(danio_orth_genes_modules, by = c("Gene stable ID version"="orths")) %>% view()


left_join(Danio_biomart, zfin_ids, by=c("Gene stable ID"="Ensembl_ID")) %>% distinct(ZFIN_ID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  left_join(danio_orth_genes_modules, by = c("Gene stable ID version"="orths")) %>% drop_na(gene) %>% filter(ZFIN_ID %in% pheno$`Gene ID`) %>% left_join(pheno, by=c("ZFIN_ID"="Gene ID")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(`Gene Symbol`,"Gene description",`Affected Structure or Process 1 superterm ID`,`Affected Structure or Process 1 superterm Name`,"Phenotype Keyword ID" , "Phenotype Keyword Name", "Publication ID", "Gene stable ID", gene) %>% filter(gene %in% cafe_genefamily_outs$genes) %>% left_join(cafe_genefamily_outs, by=c("gene"="genes"))->pheno_orth_mods


pheno_orth_mods
```

##### Global dN/dS using MG94 model
```{r}
#Parse the JSON file from HyPhy
fitmg94_json_parse<-function(orth) {
  f<-read_json(paste0("./10.HyPhy/",orth,"_fitmg94.local.json"))
  
  tibble(
    Orthogroup=orth,
    omega=f$fits$`Standard MG94`$`Rate Distributions`$`non-synonymous/synonymous rate ratio`,
    omega_ci_lb=f$fits$`Standard MG94`$`Confidence Intervals`$`non-synonymous/synonymous rate ratio`$LB,
    omega_ci_ub=f$fits$`Standard MG94`$`Confidence Intervals`$`non-synonymous/synonymous rate ratio`$UB,
    p_val=f$`test results`$`non-synonymous/synonymous rate ratio`$`p-value`,
    lrt=f$`test results`$`non-synonymous/synonymous rate ratio`$LRT) %>% 
    mutate(pval_adj=p.adjust(p_val,method = "BH"))
}

homologous_genes$genes %>%
  purrr::map(safely(fitmg94_json_parse)) %>%
  purrr::map("result") %>%       
  compact() %>% 
  list_rbind() %>% mutate(type="homologous")->fitmg94_res_homo


(genes_needed %>% distinct(Orthogroup) %>% 
    filter(!Orthogroup %in% homologous_genes$genes))$Orthogroup %>%
  purrr::map(safely(fitmg94_json_parse)) %>%
  purrr::map("result") %>%       
  compact() %>% 
  list_rbind() %>% mutate(type="non_homologous")->fitmg94_res_non_homo
```

###### Wilcox rank sum test 
```{r}

test_wil<-function(){
  
  rbind(fitmg94_res_homo %>% filter(pval_adj < 0.05) %>% slice_sample(n=200),
        fitmg94_res_non_homo %>% filter(pval_adj < 0.05) %>% slice_sample(n=200))->test_dat
  
  wilcox.test(x=test_dat %>% filter(type=="homologous") %>% pull(omega) %>% log2(),
              y=test_dat %>% filter(type=="non_homologous") %>% pull(omega) %>% log2(),
              alternative = "two.sided")->wil.res
  
  tibble(pval=wil.res$p.value,
         test=wil.res$alternative) %>% return()
  }


purrr::map(1:1000, ~test_wil()) %>% list_rbind() %>% mutate(padj=p.adjust(pval,"BH"))->global_sel_diff

```

##### FUBAR
```{r}
#Parse HyPhy output
list.files("./10.HyPhy/FUBAR/") %>% 
  str_remove_all("_cds_treeinput.fa.FUBAR.json")->og

fubar_json_parse<- function(orth) {
  f<-read_json(paste0("./10.HyPhy/FUBAR/",orth,"_cds_treeinput.fa.FUBAR.json"),
               simplifyVector = )
  headers <- map_chr(f$MLE$headers,1)
  rows <- f$MLE$content$`0`
  rows <- purrr::modify(rows, ~ modify(.x, ~ if (is.null(.x)) 0 else .x))
  sites <- f$`data partitions`$`0`$coverage
  
  purrr::map(.x = rows, 
      ~as_tibble(setNames(as.list(.x), c(headers,"q1","q2")))) %>% list_rbind() %>% 
    mutate(sites=seq(1:length(sites[[1]])),
           Orthogroup=orth) %>% 
    dplyr::select(Orthogroup,sites, everything()) %>% 
    return()
}

purrr::map(og,fubar_json_parse) %>% list_rbind()->fubar_res

homologous_genes$genes %>%
  purrr::map(safely(fubar_json_parse)) %>%
  purrr::map("result") %>%       
  compact() %>% 
  list_rbind() %>% mutate(type="homologous")->fubar_res

(genes_needed %>% distinct(Orthogroup) %>% 
    filter(!Orthogroup %in% homologous_genes$genes))$Orthogroup  %>%
  purrr::map(safely(fubar_json_parse)) %>%
  purrr::map("result") %>%       
  compact() %>% 
  list_rbind() %>% mutate(type="non_homologous")->fubar_res_non_homologous

fubar_res_non_homologous %>% mutate(selection=case_when(`Prob[alpha>beta]` > 0.9 ~ "purifying", 
                                            `Prob[alpha<beta]` > 0.9 ~"diversifying",
                                            .default = "low evidence")) %>% 
  dplyr::count(selection) %>% mutate(n.per=((n/sum(n))*100) %>% round(2)) %>% 
  mutate(selection=reorder(selection,-n.per)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=selection, y=n.per))+
  geom_col(aes(fill=selection))+
  geom_text(aes(label = n.per, y=n.per+1))+
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("#4F868C","grey80","#D92B04"))+
  labs(y="Percentage of sites", x="Selection")+
  theme_bw()->site_freq_non_homologous
```
